title: API schema to publish model capability flags, performance profiles, and stable version pinning
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: As part of the Model Onboarding initiative we need the public /models API (and internal catalog endpoints) to return machine-readable capability flags and a published performance profile for each model variant so clients and console UI can make routing, pinning, and fallback decisions.
motivation: Currently capability metadata lives in disparate places (onboarding sheets, internal docs) and the Console synthesizes a best-effort view. Customers and SDKs need a stable, versioned JSON schema that includes: feature flags (chat, function-calling, streaming, embeddings, reranking), hard limits (max_tokens, max_sequence_length), cost proxies (perf_tier), and a small performance profile object that captures P50/P95 token latency and expected throughput for common batch sizes.
proposed_change_summary:
- Add a new top-level 'capabilities' object to the /models response with explicit boolean flags and a 'features' string list.
- Add 'profile' object that includes 'context_window', 'max_tokens', 'performance_tier', 'latency_ms' map for {p50,p95} and 'throughput_rps' estimates for small/medium batches.
- Add a 'pinned_versions' list for model families where stable pins are published, including pin metadata (pin_id, pinned_at, compatible_kernels).
- Version the schema with a 'schema_version' field and maintain backwards-compatible additions only.
- Publish docs and example SDK response mapping.
acceptance_criteria:
1) /models and /internal/catalog endpoints return the new fields under schema_version '2026-03-1' for models onboarded after 2026-02-01.
2) Console shows explicit feature badges derived from capabilities flags for at least 10 curated models.
3) SDK client (python/js) can read 'pinned_versions' and prefer pinned variant when customer sets 'pin=true'.
4) No existing clients break: endpoints must still return legacy fields for one release cycle and include an opt-in header 'X-RI-ModelSchema: 2026-03-1' to receive the new structure.
5) Automated integration tests validate profile numbers are present and within sane ranges for our curated models.

implementation_notes:
- Server: runtime/service/catalog will load onboarding artifacts (YAML) and compile a normalized profile object; fallback to 'unknown' performance_tier when not present.
- Migration: support header-driven opt-in. Default behavior remains unchanged for one release.
- SDKs: add read helpers parse_model_capabilities() and prefer pinned_version if user sets client.default_pin = true.
- Console: map 'performance_tier' to color scale and expose pin management pages.
- Monitoring: create smoke job that validates top 20 models return valid profile numbers daily.
risks:
1) Benchmarks vary across hardware — publishing numbers could be misleading if not qualified; mitigated by adding 'measurement_context' and 'measurement_date'.
2) Backwards compatibility — clients might break if schema changes; mitigated by opt-in header and schema_version field.
3) Security — accidental exposure of internal telemetry; mitigated by aggregation and coarse timestamps.
